institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose SciencesPo in Paris to experience a different learning environment and live in Paris

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. Many of the websites are in French and the same applies for emails from the school. The process of selecting courses was not very transparent, but they announced that they are launching a new process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing really... But I didn't sign up for the welcome program. Others have said that the welcome program is too expensive and not worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy. I used various Facebook groups and found a nice house within the city and lived with two roommates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed it - and you can rent Velib-bikes very cheap, which makes getting around very easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is a mess (or was). At a specific time all the courses are released. Then the classes are distributed at a first-come-first-served basis. The process is very stressful when you have mandatory classes, because most were full within minutes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can attend an online class about the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get the exact ones I wanted, but they did get transferred.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare! Have backup classes ready!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The overall level was lower, but the workload is much higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depends on your classes, but I had to do a lot of presentations. The knowledge is more fact-based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Comparative politics (10 ects)
2) European integration and its challenges: the euro, migration and populism (5 ects)
3) NATO, the European Union and Ukraine: Challenges for transatlantic security in the 21st century (5 ects) 
4) Public Economics (5 ects) 
5) International Community and the Troubled Middle East (5 ects)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked public economics, International Community and the Troubled Middle East and NATO, the European Union and Ukraine. The workload was nice and they were really interesting as well

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on some trips around France that was quite nice - but also very expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation! I used Velib bike around

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There offer sports, but the spots very hard to get. There are also different clubs. I did some Model UN, which was very interesting and highly recommendable

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SPNU! They do Model UN and arrange lunches with interesting people and vists to embassies

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums are a must! And the parks are amazing. I also travelled to Rennes, Normandie, Strasbourg, Lyon and Southern France. All very recommendable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't make that many French friends, but other than that quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I attended some student climbing, where there were students as well - so sports :))

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some of the classes are very late, which we would never find in Denmark. They also eat later

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how the French appreciate aesthetics.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to enjoy the city and it is okay not to do all the school work

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The city is amazing, just being in Paris give you extra energy. And it was interesting to experience a different learning environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing work load with enjoying the city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
